frontier.title: 英伟达129亿美元收购Hugging Face+Q2营收962亿，AI软硬件生态加速闭环
frontier.desc: 9月3日英伟达宣布以129.3亿美元收购Hugging Face，获得覆盖1800万开发者、20万家企业、300万个模型的AI模型部署平台。同期英伟达FY27Q2营收962亿美元（同比+106%），数据中心收入890亿（+117%），Q3指引1080亿。AWS与英伟达计划2027-2028年部署200万张额外GPU。英伟达正从硬件与互连向AI软件生态层延伸，同时摩根大通预测2027年AI定制芯片出货量将首次超越GPU。（来源：SemiEngineering/OriginBrief/英伟达财报）

frontier.title: 博通AI半导体Q3收入167亿同比+221%，2028年剑指2300亿美元
frontier.desc: 博通FY26Q3营收296亿美元（同比+86%），其中AI半导体收入167亿美元（同比+221%、环比+54%）。CEO陈福阳给出2027财年AI收入翻倍至1150亿、2028年再翻倍至2300亿美元的指引，称定制XPU性能不输GPU且成本仅其一半。Anthropic与OpenAI将超越谷歌成为博通前两大XPU客户，2028年分别部署5GW+规模。谷歌TPU v8i量产提速、Meta MTIA系列三代迭代至2028年3GW部署。中国企业在全球ASIC前十占四席（华为昇腾、寒武纪、昆仑芯、中兴微电子）。（来源：腾讯新闻/金融投资报/华尔街见闻）

frontier.title: Intel 14A工艺良率超预期+三星Arm联合2nm端侧AI芯片：先进制程竞速升级
frontier.desc: Intel 14A（等效1.4nm）工艺缺陷密度D0已达0.5，为22nm节点以来最佳，预计2028上半年量产，较台积电A14早约半年，全面开放代工争夺苹果/谷歌/Meta订单。三星联合Arm启动2nm端侧AI SoC研发，系统LSI负责设计、代工部采用2nm制程量产，最终客户或为OpenAI。SK hynix在Nature Electronics发文指出计算吞吐量每两年翻三倍而互连带宽仅增1.4倍，存储带宽成为AI扩展瓶颈，已在印第安纳州启动HBM生产基地建设。（来源：华尔街见闻/SemiEngineering/OriginBrief）

frontier.title: SCFI七连涨至3590.05点创25个月新高：美东破10324美元，欧线九连跌
frontier.desc: 9月4日SCFI报3590.05点（+2.29%），连续第七周上涨创2024年7月以来最高。美西7242美元/FEU（+4.35%）、美东10324美元/FEU（+2.77%），美东-美西价差3082美元。东南亚893美元/TEU（+12.2%）涨幅最大。欧线2643美元/TEU（-2.69%）连续九周下跌，地中海3442美元/TEU（-3.23%）。WCI综合指数稳于4465美元/FEU，上海-洛杉矶7185美元（+5%）。亚洲14个主要港口准班率降至56.4%，为2021年1月以来最大单月降幅，平均延误6.06天。（来源：上海航运交易所/Sea-Intelligence/Drewry）

frontier.title: 美伊互相袭击油轮+伊朗拟设霍尔木兹禁区：航运风险从商业冲突升级为军事对抗
frontier.desc: 美军9月6日打击三艘伊朗油轮（含哈尔克岛附近），伊朗革命卫队海军 targeting三艘美籍油轮及另外三艘美舰。Kpler数据显示过去10天霍尔木兹日均仅10艘商船通过，创5月以来最低。伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书雷扎伊宣布将在未来几天公布霍尔木兹海峡外「禁区」，从美海军封锁线起延伸至波斯湾水域，进入者将列入伊朗制裁名单。伊朗黑名单已扩至56艘船（原油/LNG/LPG/成品油）。OPEC+维持10月产量政策不变。（来源：Reuters/Gulf News/Economic Times/HDFCSky）

life.title: 布伦特逼近97美元、WTI破92：美伊油轮互击推升油价冲击百元大关
life.desc: 9月7日布伦特原油期货涨0.54%报96.80美元/桶，WTI涨0.72%报92.14美元/桶。上周布伦特累涨7.8%、WTI累涨近10%。美军打击伊朗油轮及伊朗反击美籍油轮后，霍尔木兹海峡日均仅10艘商船通过创5月新低。摩根大通估计每多中断一个月油价或涨7-8美元/桶，若持续三个月布伦特均值或达114美元。高盛警告霍尔木兹长期中断可推布伦特至120美元。OPEC+维持10月产量不变。国内航煤出厂价8170元/吨（同比+45.76%），对航空物流成本端形成持续压力。（来源：Reuters/Economic Times/JPMorgan/Goldman Sachs）

life.title: 金价回落至4393美元/盎司：非农超预期强化加息押注，无息资产承压
life.desc: 9月7日现货黄金报4393.74美元/盎司（-0.82%），COMEX期金4477.20美元（周跌1.16%）。国内AU9999报949元/克。美国8月非农新增16.2万人远超预期5.6万，失业率4.1%，利率期货对9月加息押注升至约60%。美元指数走强压制贵金属。但中东地缘风险与油价上涨强化通胀黏性预期，形成「油价涨→通胀→加息→金价承压」的传导链。市场聚焦本周8月CPI数据——若超预期将进一步打压降息预期。（来源：金投网/金价查询网/东方财富/陆家嘴财经早餐）

life.title: LME铜创历史收盘新高14415美元/吨，锌价逼近四年高位3946美元
life.desc: 9月4日LME期铜收涨0.6%报14415美元/吨创收盘历史新高，期锌涨0.9%报3946美元/吨（周涨1.6%）。美国7月精炼铜进口达225094公吨创1990年来单月纪录，COMEX铜库存连续53天升至764597短吨历史高位，因交易商抢在潜在铜关税前大量运入。关税不确定性使COMEX与LME/SHFE库存出现区域性溢价。中东地缘冲突推高油价与通胀担忧，对工业金属需求端形成多空交织。LME期铝3293美元/吨（-0.5%）、期镍16846美元/吨（+0.4%）、期锡54866美元/吨（-0.2%）。（来源：MoneyDJ/中国金融信息网/东方财富）

growth.title: 《The Box: How the Shipping Container Made the World Smaller》— Marc Levinson
growth.desc: Marc Levinson经典著作，讲述集装箱如何重塑全球贸易与供应链。本周SCFI七连涨至3590点、亚洲港口准班率降至56.4%、霍尔木兹日均仅10艘商船通过——这些现象的根源都在于集装箱化带来的效率革命与其物理与地缘瓶颈。建议结合本周拥堵与军事冲突新闻重读第11章「瓶颈与反弹」，理解为什么效率越高、系统越脆弱、恢复时间越长。

growth.title: 思考框架：霍尔木兹禁区+巴拿马限流双瓶颈下的全球运力再分配决策树
growth.desc: 本周伊朗宣布将在霍尔木兹海峡外设立禁区，巴拿马运河9月15日降至32艘/日、10月1日吃水47.5英尺。构建运力再分配决策树：①波斯湾/中东线货→评估好望角绕行（+12-15天）或暂停发货②美东线货→苏伊士+美东（红海风险仍存）或美西+IPI（价差3082美元/FEU可覆盖内陆铁路）③欧线货→苏伊士复航中、20000TEU大船过剩，9月底或触底④东南亚→台风后舱位紧张+12.2%涨幅，提前2-3周订舱。决策关键变量：客户对7-15天缓冲的容忍度+保险费率（战争险已从0.25%飙至12%）。

growth.title: The Freightos Freight Market Update Podcast — 2026 Week 36: SCFI Seven-Week Streak & Hormuz Blacklist
growth.desc: Freightos研究主管Judah Levine主持的周度运价播客最新集聚焦SCFI七连涨与霍尔木兹黑名单升级。核心要点：8月货运量在5月底旺季提前启动后仍延续强劲，承运人通过空白航行与航线调整维持定价权，9月小幅增舱但10月黄金周将再空白。电商卖家加速出货以赶10月中下旬入仓截止日。对物流经理的启发：Freightos Baltic Index（FBX）与SCFI的价差是判断现货vs长约优劣的关键指标，本周FBX美东较SCFI溢价约8%，说明现货市场更紧张。

growth.title: 全球港口准班率监控看板（Sea-Intelligence / Kpler双数据源）
growth.desc: 建议建立每周跟踪看板：①Sea-Intelligence全球准班率（本周56.4%，2021年1月以来最大单月降幅）②亚洲14港待泊船数与平均延误（本周6.06天）③Kpler霍尔木兹日均通行商船数（本周10艘/天创5月新低）④SCFI七连涨斜率与WCI-LME铜价差（铜创新高暗示制造业需求韧性强于预期）⑤伊朗黑名单船舶数（56艘且持续扩大）。本周关键信号：准班率从62.5%到56.4%的单月降幅创4年纪录，而平均延误从5.47天增至6.06天，说明拥堵从「船等泊位」恶化为「系统级延误级联」，Q4恢复窗口已缩短至6-8周。

growth.title: Coursera: Supply Chain Logistics（Rutgers University, Rudolf Leuschner教授）
growth.desc: 罗格斯大学供应链物流入门课程，覆盖运输模式选择、仓储网络设计、库存策略与物流成本优化。与MIT SC2x形成互补——Rutgers侧重实务操作与案例分析，MIT侧重数学建模。本周美东10324 vs 美西7242 vs 欧线2643美元的价差结构、霍尔木兹禁区对中东线运力再分配的冲击、东南亚893美元/TEU单周涨12.2%——正是课程中运输模式与路径选择章节的现实案例：如何用Excel Solver求解多约束最优路径。9月开学季适合系统补基础，4周可完成。

insights.title: SCFI七连涨+准班率创4年最大单月降幅：运力约束从周期性走向系统性
insights.content: 9月4日SCFI七连涨至3590.05点创25个月新高，但更值得关注的信号是Sea-Intelligence数据：全球集装箱船准班率7月降至56.4%，较上月下降6.1个百分点，为2021年1月以来最大单月降幅。平均延误攀升至6.06天。亚洲14个最繁忙港口的准班率全部下降，上海与宁波因连续台风叠加拥堵严重。这不再是周期性天气扰动，而是系统性瓶颈：①巴拿马运河9月15日降至32艘/日、10月1日吃水47.5英尺，这是百年工程级物理限制；②霍尔木兹海峡日均仅10艘商船通过创5月新低，伊朗即将公布禁区使商业油轮成为军事对抗工具；③船公司虽新增20000TEU大船，但集中投放欧线导致欧线九连跌（-2.69%），美东/美西/东南亚反而面临结构性运力不足。对物流经理实操建议：①Q4圣诞货须在9月15日前完成美东订舱（10月1日巴拿马吃水进一步收紧将再推GRI）；②美西+IPI替代方案价差3082美元/FEU，但需确认BNSF/UP铁路运能；③欧线客户利用大船过剩谈判长约折扣，9月底或触底；④东南亚单周+12.2%，9-10月有进一步涨价预期，提前2-3周订舱。参考判断。

insights.title: 英伟达收购Hugging Face与博通连续翻番指引：AI算力民主化加速但物流成本隐忧浮现
insights.content: 英伟达129亿美元收购Hugging Face（1800万开发者生态），博通FY26Q3 AI半导体167亿美元同比+221%，指引2027年1150亿、2028年2300亿连续翻番。中国企业全球ASIC前十占四席。但被忽视的是物流成本端传导：①台积电、SK hynix先进封装产能集中在台湾与韩国，台海地缘风险下「AI芯片海峡通道」日均通过VLCC价值超10亿美元；②SEMI报告全球晶圆设备支出2026年同比+18%集中在先进制程，设备运输温控/防震/安保标准提升使特种柜运费较普通柜高3-5倍；③美国7月精炼铜进口创纪录225094吨抢在关税前运入，COMEX铜库存53连升至历史高位764597短吨，说明全球制造业正提前布局「关税壁垒前物流冲刺」，与圣诞备货旺季共振，加剧跨太平洋舱位紧张。对物流经理建议：①AI服务器/芯片特种运输SOP需在9月更新，纳入台海替代路径（釜山/新加坡中转）；②关注COMEX与LME铜价差作为全球制造业物流需求的前瞻指标；③评估「关税冲刺」对Q4跨太平洋舱位的挤压效应。参考判断。

insights.title: 霍尔木兹禁区+美伊油轮互击：原油逼近百元对物流全链路成本的级联传导
insights.content: 9月7日布伦特逼近97美元、WTI破92美元，美军打击三艘伊朗油轮（含哈尔克岛附近），伊朗反击美籍油轮并即将公布霍尔木兹外禁区。Kpler数据过去10天日均仅10艘商船通过霍尔木兹创5月新低。摩根大通估计每多中断一月油价或涨7-8美元，若持续三个月布伦特均值或达114美元。高盛警告长期中断可推至120美元。对物流全链路的级联传导：①燃油附加费（BAF）：船公司燃油成本占比约30-40%，布伦特从80→97美元意味着BAF或再涨15-20%，9月底10月初新一轮FAF调整窗口；②保险费率：战争险已从0.25%飙至12%，霍尔木兹航线全险成本可能达运价30-50%；③空运替代：油价上涨使航空煤油出厂价已达8170元/吨（+45.76%），空运运价BAI00同比+18.1%——美东/中东线高价值货的空运替代成本优势正在收窄；④铁路替代：中欧班列（12-16天）对欧线货的吸引力上升，但霍尔木兹局势不影响中亚陆桥，可作为中东货的替代路径（经哈萨克斯坦-土库曼斯坦-伊朗北部陆桥）。建议物流经理：①重新核算Q4各航线全成本（运价+BAF+保险+缓冲时间成本）；②将霍尔木兹通过量纳入每周运力监控看板；③评估中欧班列舱位锁定窗口。参考判断。

email.body:
Dear [Client Name],

I am writing to alert you to a rapidly escalating situation in the Strait of Hormuz that will materially impact your shipping costs and routing options for Q4.

Over the past weekend, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers — including one near Kharg Island, Iran's key export hub — and Iran's IRGC Navy retaliated by targeting three US-linked oil tankers as well as three additional US vessels. Data from Kpler shows that only 10 commodity vessels per day transited the Strait over the past 10 days, the lowest level since May. Furthermore, Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced it will declare an exclusion zone extending from the US naval blockade line into the Persian Gulf in the coming days, with any entering vessel placed on Iran's sanctions list.

The market impact has been immediate:

• Brent crude has risen to approximately $96.80/barrel (+7.8% last week); WTI at $92.14/barrel (+10% last week). JPMorgan estimates every additional month of disruption could add $7–8/barrel.
• War risk insurance premiums have surged from 0.25% to as high as 12% of vessel value on Hormuz-routed cargo.
• SCFI has risen for seven consecutive weeks to 3,590.05 points — a 25-month high — with US East Coast rates at $10,324/FEU and Southeast Asia up 12.2% in a single week to $893/TEU.

To protect your Q4 supply chain, I recommend the following actions:

1. For Middle East/Persian Gulf cargo: evaluate rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope (+12–15 days transit) or suspending non-urgent shipments until the exclusion zone parameters are clarified. If you have cargo on the water, confirm your carrier's insurance coverage and surcharge structure immediately.

2. For US East Coast cargo: finalize all bookings before September 15, when Panama Canal transits drop further to 32 vessels/day. Accept the GRI and Panama surcharges — the cost of waiting is now higher than the cost of acting. The East–West spread of $3,082/FEU may justify USWC + IPI routing, subject to inland rail capacity.

3. For Europe-bound cargo: carriers are deploying surplus 20,000+ TEU vessels, pushing Europe rates down for nine consecutive weeks to $2,643/TEU. Use this window to negotiate contract discounts before Q4 demand recovery.

4. For all shipments via Hormuz-affected lanes: expect a 15–20% increase in Bunker Adjustment Factor (BAF) at the next adjustment window in late September/early October. Build this into your Q4 logistics budget now.

5. For time-sensitive, high-value cargo to the Middle East or Europe: consider the China-Europe Railway Express (12–16 days transit) as an alternative that bypasses both Hormuz and Panama constraints.

I am monitoring the situation hourly and will provide an updated advisory as soon as the exclusion zone boundaries are formally announced. I would welcome a call this week to review your Q4 booking plan and adjust your routing strategy accordingly.

Best regards,
Raymond
Global Logistics Manager

email.body:
Dear [Client Name],

I am writing to alert you to a critical development in global container shipping that will directly impact your Q4 supply chain planning.

As of this week, global port congestion has reached an unprecedented 4.3 million TEU of stranded capacity, exceeding the previous pandemic peak of 4.0 million TEU recorded in 2022. The SCFI composite index has risen for six consecutive weeks to 3,509.54 points, a 25-month high. Key lane developments:

• US East Coast: $10,046/FEU (+3.57%), driven by Panama Canal transit cuts to 32 vessels/day from September 15 and tightening draft limits to 47.5 feet from October 1.
• US West Coast: $6,940/FEU (+2.58%), with spot quotes for early September already at $7,500–7,700/FEU.
• South America: $9,438/FEU (+15.36% in a single week), the sharpest increase across all lanes.
• Europe: $2,716/TEU (-4.43%), weakening due to oversupply of 20,000+ TEU vessels.

The structural nature of this congestion—port infrastructure has not kept pace with fleet expansion to 34.4 million TEU—means the current tightness is unlikely to resolve before year-end.

To protect your Q4 shipments, I recommend the following actions:

1. Finalize all US East Coast bookings before September 15, before the second Panama transit reduction takes effect and carriers implement the next wave of GRI ($500–700/FEU) plus Panama surcharges ($200–400/FEU).
2. Evaluate US West Coast + IPI routing as a cost alternative. The current East–West spread of approximately $3,000/FEU often offsets the inland rail leg, but confirm BNSF/UP capacity availability first.
3. Lock South America rates immediately—this lane is experiencing the fastest price acceleration and tightest space conditions.
4. For Europe-bound cargo, delay booking until late September to capture potential seasonal lows, as carriers are struggling to fill 20,000+ TEU vessels and may offer contract discounts.
5. Build in 7–10 days of buffer for Christmas-season cargo, given that current congestion levels already exceed 2022 pandemic peaks in absolute terms.

I would welcome a call this week to review your Q4 lane-by-lane booking plan and identify the optimal routing mix for each destination.

Best regards,
Raymond
Global Logistics Manager

sentences.title: Smartphones in Schools: Should They Be Banned?
sentences.text:
Walk into almost any high school today and you will see the same scene. Before class begins, students are looking at their phones. During breaks, they scroll through short videos or send messages to friends. Even during class, some students check their screens under the desk. Smartphones have become a part of students' daily lives, and they have also become one of the biggest challenges for modern teachers.

Many schools around the world have decided to ban phones in the classroom. France, for example, passed a law in 2018 that forbids students under 15 from using phones in schools. In the United Kingdom, some schools ask students to submit their phones at the door each morning. The main reason is simple: phones are distracting. A ringing phone or a quick look at messages can pull attention away from the teacher. Some studies have shown that students who use phones in class often remember less of what they learn.

However, phones are not always bad. Many experts argue that phones can also be useful learning tools. With a phone, students can look up new words in seconds, watch short educational videos, and join online group projects. During a science class, for example, students can record their experiments and share results with classmates. Phones also help students who cannot easily come to school to stay connected with their class through live video.

The answer is not the same for every country or every school. Some schools lock phones away during lessons but allow students to use them at lunch or after class. Other schools permit phones as long as students follow clear rules, such as keeping them in their bags. What most teachers agree on is that phones change the way students communicate — and that schools need to teach young people how to manage their online lives.

The same ban may work in one country but fail in another. France's rule targets students under 15; in many Chinese middle schools, students may bring phones but must keep them away during class. In Finland, where students rank among the world's top performers, teachers trust students to manage phones on their own. There is no single perfect answer. What matters most is whether students can learn to control themselves.

In conclusion, the question of banning phones is really a question of discipline. Technology itself is not good or bad — it is a tool, and a tool depends on the hands that hold it. Schools need to find a balance: protect focused learning while still helping students develop healthy digital habits. The goal is not to remove technology from young lives, but to teach students how to use it wisely.

sentences.title: The Words That Shape Young Minds: Why Praise Style Matters
sentences.text:
When a student brings home a test paper, what does a teacher or parent usually say? Many adults will say, "You are so smart!" or "You are a natural talent!" This kind of praise feels kind, but new research in education shows that how we praise children may matter as much as the praise itself.

For years, studies have compared two kinds of praise. The first kind focuses on the child's intelligence: "You are so clever!" The second kind focuses on the child's effort: "I can see how hard you worked on this!" Children who are praised for effort often keep working when the task becomes hard. Children who are praised for being smart often stop trying because they are afraid of looking less clever.

So why does the same word "effort" change how a child responds? The answer lies in the idea of feedback. A feedback that praises intelligence tells the child, "You did well because you were born smart." A feedback that praises effort tells the child, "You did well because you tried hard, and you can try again." One feedback closes the door to improvement; the other opens it.

This idea helps us understand student motivation in daily life. When a student says, "I am just bad at math," it often means he or she has been praised the wrong way for years. The student has learned to avoid hard tasks to protect his or her image. Teachers who give specific feedback — such as "You used a smart method here" or "Try checking step three again" — usually see stronger performance than those who simply say "Good job."

Of course, not every student responds in the same way. Some students struggle with behavior problems, family stress, or learning difficulties. In these cases, the balance between praise and correction becomes even more important. A critic who only points out mistakes can make a student lose hope; an adult who only gives praise without honesty may keep a student from growing.

The good news is that good feedback can be learned. A parent can try saying, "I am proud of how you kept trying." A teacher can write "Your ideas are becoming clearer" instead of "Great work." Over time, these small changes can motivate students to achieve more, because they feel that their effort — not just their intelligence — is what truly matches success.

In short, the right words at the right time can shape how a young person sees himself or herself for years. As teachers, parents, and friends, we should become more aware of how our words work. Honest, specific, and natural feedback is one of the simplest and strongest tools we have to help students grow.

sentences.translation:
当学生把试卷带回家时，老师或家长通常会说什么？很多成年人会说："你真聪明！"或"你真是天生的好苗子！"这种表扬听起来很善意，但教育领域的新研究表明，我们表扬孩子的方式可能和表扬本身一样重要。
多年来，研究已经比较了两种表扬方式。第一种聚焦于孩子的智力："你真聪明！"第二种聚焦于孩子的努力："我能看出你为此付出了多少！"因努力而受表扬的孩子在任务变难时往往继续努力。因聪明而受表扬的孩子则常常停止尝试，因为他们害怕自己显得不够聪明。
那么，为什么同一个"努力"之词会改变一个孩子的反应？答案藏在"反馈"这一概念里。表扬智力的反馈告诉孩子："你做得好是因为你天生聪明。"表扬努力的反馈则告诉孩子："你做得好是因为你努力了，你可以再试一次。"一种反馈关上了通往进步的门，而另一种则打开了它。
这一理念有助于我们理解学生日常的学习动机。当一个学生说"我就是学不好数学"时，往往意味着他/她多年来被以错误的方式表扬过。这个学生已经学会回避困难任务，以保护自己的形象。给出具体反馈的老师——例如"你这里的方法很聪明"或"试着再检查第三步"——通常比那些只说"干得好"的老师能看到学生更强的表现。
当然，并不是每个学生的反应都一样。有些学生在行为问题、家庭压力或学习困难中挣扎。在这些情境下，表扬与纠错之间的平衡就更加重要。一个只指出错误的批评者可能让学生失去希望；而一个只表扬却不诚实的成年人，则可能让学生无法真正成长。
好消息是，好的反馈是可以学习的。家长可以试着说"我为你一直坚持努力而骄傲"。老师可以写"你的思路越来越清晰"，而不是只写"做得好"。日积月累，这些小变化能激励学生取得更大成就，因为他们会感到：真正与成功相配的，是他们的努力——而不仅仅是智力。
简而言之，恰当的时机说恰当的话，可以塑造一个年轻人看待自己的方式，长达多年。作为老师、家长和朋友，我们都应该更加意识到话语的作用。诚实、具体、自然的反馈，是我们帮助学生成长所能使用的最简单也最有力的工具之一。
sentences.analysis: 重点掌握核心词汇（teacher/parent/praise/feedback/intelligence/effort/respond/motivation/specific/performance/struggle/behavior/balance/critic/mistake/motivate/aware/natural/match 等），理解"表扬努力比表扬智力更能激发学生动机"这一教育心理学命题。句式以简单句 + while 表对比 + because 原因状从为主，适合 CET4 精读训练。建议先速读抓主旨（praise style matters），再精读段落定位"one feedback closes the door; the other opens it"这一关键对比，最后用 one... the other... 句式仿写"两种教育方式的差异"段落。

sentences.title: Street Markets: The Soul of a City
sentences.text:
In cities around the world, there is a place where the heart of local life can still be felt. It is neither a museum nor a shopping mall — it is the street market. Here, vendors call out their prices, the smell of fresh food fills the air, and people of all ages come together. For centuries, street markets have served as one of the most important social spaces in human cities.

Every market has its own flavor. In Thailand, vendors sell spicy noodles from small wooden stalls. In Morocco, buyers and sellers bargain over colorful spices and silver jewelry. In southern China, morning markets are filled with fresh vegetables, live fish, and the sounds of greeting. Each market is a living example of a city's culture and daily rhythm.

For many tourists, a street market is the highlight of any trip. They wander through narrow paths, looking at things they have never seen before. For local people, however, the market is far more than a place to buy food. It is a place to meet neighbors, exchange news, and share a few words with the vendor they have known for years. Children learn to count money here, and old people come to feel they still belong to the city. Even a quiet spot under a tree can become a small stage for everyday life.

Modern life, however, is changing these markets. Large supermarkets and online shopping apps now supply most of what people need at home. Many young people prefer to order food with a phone, instead of carrying bags home from a crowded market. As a result, some old markets have slowly disappeared, and the small spirit that once filled them seems harder to find.

But not everyone agrees that this change is for the better. Some city leaders now try to preserve these markets as part of their cultural heritage. They connect old markets with tourism, art festivals, and food tours. A growing number of young chefs and small business owners choose to set up their stalls in traditional markets, hoping to keep the spirit of the place alive. Digital tools have even tried to copy the experience through online live-streaming, but they cannot replace the warmth of a real handshake or the joy of a good bargain.

In conclusion, street markets are more than places to buy and sell. They are living museums of a city's culture, where strangers can become friends in a single conversation. Whether you are a tourist looking for adventure or a local looking for a good bargain, the street market will always remain the soul of a city.
sentences.keywords: vendor (/ˈvendər/ n.) ；stall (/stɔːl/ n.) ；flavor (/ˈfleɪvər/ n.) ；bargain (/ˈbɑːrɡən/ v./n.) ；fresh (/freʃ/ adj.) ；culture (/ˈkʌltʃər/ n.) ；daily (/ˈdeɪli/ adj.) ；tourist (/ˈtʊrɪst/ n.) ；neighbor (/ˈneɪbər/ n.) ；crowded (/ˈkraʊdɪd/ adj.) ；supply (/səˈplaɪ/ v./n.) ；preserve (/prɪˈzɜːrv/ v.) ；connect (/kəˈnekt/ v.) ；spirit (/ˈspɪrɪt/ n.) ；wander (/ˈwɑːndər/ v.)
sentences.translation:
在世界各大城市里，有一个地方仍能让人感受到本地生活的脉搏。它既不是博物馆，也不是大型商场——它就是街头市场。在这里，小贩们高声叫卖价格，新鲜食物的香气弥漫在空气中，各年龄层的人们聚集在一起。几百年来，街头市场一直是人类城市中最重要的公共空间之一。
每个市场都有自己独特的风味。在泰国，小贩们从一个个小木摊位上售卖香辣的面条。在摩洛哥，买家和卖家讨价还价，议价的对象是五颜六色的香料和银饰。在中国南方，晨间市场里摆满了新鲜蔬菜、活鱼和此起彼伏的招呼声。每一个市场都是一座城市文化与日常节奏的鲜活体现。
对许多游客而言，街头市场是任何旅程中的亮点。他们在狭窄的小道间漫步，浏览从未见过的各种物件。然而，对当地人而言，市场远不止是一个买东西的地方。它是与邻居相会、互通消息、与相熟多年的小贩聊几句的场所。孩子们在这里学会数钱，老人们在这里找回仍属于这座城市的感觉。即便是大树下的一小块静谧之处，也可以成为日常生活的小小舞台。
然而，现代生活正在改变这些市场。大型超市和线上购物应用如今能「供给」大多数家庭所需的物品。许多年轻人更喜欢用手机下单点餐，而不愿从拥挤的市场把大袋小袋拎回家。于是，一些老市场逐渐消失了，曾经弥漫其中的那股鲜活的精神似乎也越来越难寻觅。
但并非所有人都认同这种变化是积极的。一些城市管理者如今致力于将这些市场作为文化遗产加以「保护」。他们将老市场与旅游业、艺术节、美食之旅「连接」起来。越来越多的年轻厨师和小企业主选择把摊位设在传统市场中，希望延续这个地方的精神气质。数字工具甚至试图通过线上直播来复制这种体验，却无法替代一次真实握手所传递的温暖，也无法复制讨价还价所带来的乐趣。
总之，街头市场远不止是买卖的场所。它们是一座城市文化的活博物馆，陌生人也能在一次交谈中变成朋友。无论你是想体验冒险的游客，还是想买到实惠好物的本地人，街头市场都会是一座城市永远的「灵魂」。
sentences.analysis: 重点掌握核心词汇（vendor/stall/flavor/bargain/culture/tourist/spirit/preserve/connect/crowded 等），理解「街头市场 = 城市灵魂」这一文化命题及其在现代化进程中的张力。句式以简单句 + there be 句型 + where 定语从句 + 让步状从为主，适合 CET4 精读训练。建议先速读抓主旨（市场是城市的灵魂 vs 现代化冲击），再精读段落定位关键对比句（For tourists vs For local people），最后用 far more than... 句式仿写一段关于传统场所保护的小议论文。
